correctness.rationale: The original smooth gradient potential on the fixed-mean hyperplane becomes an exact quadratic-minus-two-log-cosh energy in path differences. Its Hessian is a rank-two perturbation with largest eigenvalue (K+sqrt((K-2)^2+4))/2. For alpha <= its reciprocal, convexity (and an exact strict radial inequality at equality) gives uniqueness and global gradient convergence. Above it coercivity yields nonzero minima; absolute-value improvement forces uniform-sign differences, and strict tanh subhomogeneity gives a unique positive solution. Perron contraction yields positive-definite Hessian and local exponential stability. Tested 750 finite numerical assertions from the supplied CHECK.py against the analytical formulas; tests are supplementary, not infinite certification.

value.rationale: The originating study explicitly leaves an exact interval for this natural two-hostile-edge configuration. The theorem gives a sharp all-population-size critical value, a complete nonlinear description of global preferred polarized outcomes, and the unexpected all-strength invariance of total opinion range to the position of the hostile path tie. This distinguishes topology of force placement from severity of global polarization under a precise model, with exact all-size assumptions; it is more than a generic signed-Laplacian observation or narrow numerical improvement.
